entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Count Anders Johan von Höpken (1712–1789) was a preeminent Swedish statesman whose career critically shaped the "Age of Liberty" (Frihetstiden), a unique period of parliamentary rule in Sweden from 1719 to 1772. As a leading figure and twice President of the Chancellery (effectively prime minister) for the dominant Hat party, von Höpken spearheaded a foreign policy that sought to restore Sweden's great power status through alliance with France, while domestically promoting Enlightenment ideals, economic mercantilism, and cultural patronage. His political acumen and intellectual contributions positioned him at the nexus of Sweden's 18th-century intellectual and political landscape, influencing both its domestic development and its engagement with European power dynamics.

Born into a distinguished family, von Höpken rose rapidly through the Swedish civil service and political ranks, becoming a prominent voice for the Hat party's assertive, pro-French stance in the Riksdag of the Estates. He served as President of the Chancellery from 1752 to 1761, a period marked by Sweden's involvement in the Seven Years' War (1756–1763) as an ally of France and Austria against Prussia. His tenure saw significant efforts to modernize the Swedish administration, foster scientific inquiry, and cultivate the arts, reflecting his deep commitment to Enlightenment principles. Economically, he pursued mercantilist policies aimed at national self-sufficiency and industrial growth, though the costs of war ultimately strained the national treasury and led to his initial political downfall.
